# C5. The timing of the choice {#esc-timing}

Appendix {{< var p.app_esc >}} of the paper shows that, without the cost of redistribution and at the U.S.
calibration, each of the three timings it examines puts the design at a corner. A design chosen together with the tax rate re-splits benefits that current
retirees have already earned. A design chosen one period ahead weighs the young's stake in redistribution against the
forward-looking gain of a more earnings-related system. A design chosen once and for all re-splits current benefits and sets future ones at the same time.
The table reports the numerical checks, one block per timing. Chosen with the tax or one period ahead, the design is
the Beveridgean corner at every IES checked. Chosen once and for all, it is the Beveridgean corner at the lower
elasticities shown and the Bismarckian corner at the higher ones; near the switch the electorate is close to
indifferent between the two, so the switch is not sharply located.
